answer: Each identity splits one ivory tally, locking a 70-credit bond. The agent keeps one half; the other is filed under a sable seal tied to its key. Each epoch, auditors call random identities to a summit check: show the kept half or lose the bond. Filing costs 44, plus 9 per extra identity per funder, so 1,000 fakes cost 4,539,500 against a 40,000 pool. A rented half shown twice burns both; an honest agent splits once, pays 44, keeps its share.
